formulas.name: The Specific Loss
formulas.template: I lost {amount or time} because of {small, avoidable thing}.
formulas.example: I wasted four months on a portfolio nobody opened.
formulas.purpose: Stakes and honesty in one line. The viewer stays to learn the avoidable thing.
formulas.ruins: A vague loss ('I lost a lot'), or never naming the thing.

formulas.name: The Receipt
formulas.template: In {time} I went from {A} to {B}. One change did it.
formulas.example: In 90 days I went from 12 views a video to 40,000. One change did it.
formulas.purpose: Proof first, method second. Works when the numbers are real and checkable.
formulas.ruins: Numbers you cannot back up. Hiding the one change until the end.

formulas.name: Nobody Tells You
formulas.template: Nobody tells you {truth about this stage}.
formulas.example: Nobody tells you the first thirty videos are practice.
formulas.purpose: Insider permission. The viewer feels they are getting what the guides left out.
formulas.ruins: Using it for something everybody already says.

formulas.name: The Contrarian Flip
formulas.template: {Popular advice} is wrong. Do {opposite} instead.
formulas.example: Posting every day is slowing your channel down. Post twice a week and do this instead.
formulas.purpose: Pattern interrupt. Disagreeing with a belief the viewer holds forces a decision to stay.
formulas.ruins: A flip with no evidence or no better alternative.

formulas.name: The Biggest Mistake
formulas.template: The biggest mistake {audience} make with {topic} is {x}.
formulas.example: The biggest mistake first-year students make with scholarships is applying late.
formulas.purpose: Self-diagnosis. People watch to check whether they are making it.
formulas.ruins: A mistake nobody actually makes.

formulas.name: The Numbered List
formulas.template: {N} {things} I wish I knew before {milestone}.
formulas.example: Five things I wish I knew before my first cybersecurity interview.
formulas.purpose: A visible finish line. The viewer knows how long the payoff takes.
formulas.ruins: Padding to hit the number. A list with no strongest item first.

formulas.name: The Statistic
formulas.template: {X}% of {group} {surprising behavior}.
formulas.example: Nine out of ten applicants never read the scholarship rules.
formulas.purpose: A number the viewer wants to be on the right side of.
formulas.ruins: An invented or unsourced figure.

formulas.name: The Compressed Timeline
formulas.template: How I {result} in {short time} with {constraint}.
formulas.example: How I learned enough networking to pass an exam in 21 days with no bootcamp.
formulas.purpose: Promises a method inside a constraint. The constraint is what makes it feel possible.
formulas.ruins: A timeline you did not actually hit.

formulas.name: The Warning
formulas.template: Do not {action} until you know {thing}.
formulas.example: Do not send your visa documents until you check this one stamp.
formulas.purpose: Loss aversion. A warning is more urgent than a tip.
formulas.ruins: A warning with nothing at stake.

formulas.name: The Hidden Mechanism
formulas.template: Here is why {phenomenon} really happens.
formulas.example: Here is why your best videos get the fewest views in the first hour.
formulas.purpose: Explains something the viewer has seen but could not explain.
formulas.ruins: An explanation that is just a restatement.

formulas.name: Before and After
formulas.template: Before: {pain}. After: {gain}. The difference was {one change}.
formulas.example: Before: forty edits per video. After: six. The difference was one template.
formulas.purpose: A clear contrast the viewer can picture.
formulas.ruins: No believable bridge between the two states.

formulas.name: The Callout
formulas.template: If you are a {specific person} who {specific situation}, watch this.
formulas.example: If you are applying abroad with a family budget, this is the order to do things in.
formulas.purpose: Filters in the right viewer and tells everyone else to move on, which raises retention.
formulas.ruins: A callout so broad it names everyone.

formulas.name: The Confession
formulas.template: I am embarrassed to admit I {did X}.
formulas.example: I am embarrassed to admit I failed my first security lab three times.
formulas.purpose: Lowers the viewer's guard. Honesty reads as credibility.
formulas.ruins: A fake flaw that is really a brag.

formulas.name: I Tried It So You Do Not Have To
formulas.template: I tried {thing} for {time} so you do not have to.
formulas.example: I tried waking at 5am for thirty days so you do not have to.
formulas.purpose: Borrowed experience. The viewer gets the result without the cost.
formulas.ruins: Reporting a result you did not actually test.

formulas.name: Unpopular Opinion
formulas.template: Unpopular opinion: {claim}.
formulas.example: Unpopular opinion: most coding tutorials teach you to copy, not to think.
formulas.purpose: Invites agreement or argument, both of which are engagement.
formulas.ruins: An opinion nobody disagrees with.

formulas.name: The Question With Teeth
formulas.template: Why do {group} always {surprising behavior}?
formulas.example: Why do the best students quietly stop using the library?
formulas.purpose: A question the viewer cannot answer in their head, so they wait for it.
formulas.ruins: A yes or no question. A question you answer in the next sentence.

formulas.name: What They Will Not Tell You
formulas.template: What {authority} will not tell you about {topic}.
formulas.example: What universities will not tell you about hidden fees.
formulas.purpose: Taps distrust of institutions. Strong, but only if the reveal is real.
formulas.ruins: Teasing a secret that turns out to be common knowledge.
rx: \b(won'?t|will not|don'?t want you to|doesn'?t want you to)\s+(tell|know|say)

formulas.name: The Myth Bust
formulas.template: You have been told {myth}. Here is what actually happens.
formulas.example: You have been told hashtags get you reach. Here is what actually happens.
formulas.purpose: Replaces a belief with a better one. Strong for educational channels.
formulas.ruins: Busting a myth nobody believed.
rx: \b(myth|you'?ve been told|you were told|everyone says|they say)\b

formulas.name: The Clock
formulas.template: You have {time} to {action} before {consequence}.
formulas.example: You have twelve days to claim this before the deadline closes.
formulas.purpose: A real deadline creates a reason to watch now.
formulas.ruins: A fake deadline. Viewers learn quickly.

formulas.name: The Teardown
formulas.template: I broke down why {thing} got {number} views.
formulas.example: I broke down why this explainer got two million views with no face on screen.
formulas.purpose: Lets the viewer borrow a pattern that already worked.
formulas.ruins: Praising the thing instead of finding the mechanism.

formulas.name: The Shortcut
formulas.template: The fastest way to {outcome} if you are {constraint}.
formulas.example: The fastest way to learn Linux if you only have evenings.
formulas.purpose: Speaks to impatience and a real limit on time or money.
formulas.ruins: A shortcut that skips the hard part without saying so.

formulas.name: The Cold Open
formulas.template: {Time and place}. I was {doing something ordinary} when {the unexpected thing}.
formulas.example: Last March. I was submitting a form when the portal refused my passport.
formulas.purpose: Starts inside a scene. The viewer wants to know what happens.
formulas.ruins: Scene-setting that takes more than one sentence.

formulas.name: Head to Head
formulas.template: {A} vs {B}: I tested both for {time}.
formulas.example: Paper notes vs a tablet: I tested both for a full semester.
formulas.purpose: Built-in tension. The viewer picks a side before the answer.
formulas.ruins: A comparison with no clear criteria.

formulas.name: The Beginner Trap
formulas.template: If you are just starting {skill}, avoid {trap}.
formulas.example: If you are just starting with cybersecurity, avoid buying five courses.
formulas.purpose: Protects a vulnerable viewer. Trust builds fast.
formulas.ruins: Warning against something that is not actually a trap.

formulas.name: You Do Not Need It
formulas.template: You do not need {thing people think they need} to {outcome}.
formulas.example: You do not need a camera upgrade to make videos people finish.
formulas.purpose: Removes a barrier. High share rate among beginners.
formulas.ruins: Telling people they do not need something they really do need.

formulas.name: The One Thing
formulas.template: If I could teach only one thing about {topic}, it would be {x}.
formulas.example: If I could teach only one thing about interviews, it would be the first ninety seconds.
formulas.purpose: Forces prioritisation. The viewer gets the 80 percent.
formulas.ruins: Naming one thing and then listing five.

formulas.name: The Exact Process
formulas.template: This is my exact {process} for {outcome}.
formulas.example: This is my exact checklist for turning one video into five posts.
formulas.purpose: Specific and replicable, which is rare enough to earn saves.
formulas.ruins: Calling it exact and then being vague.

formulas.name: The Named Rule
formulas.template: The {N}-{unit} rule for {situation}.
formulas.example: The ten-minute rule for starting work you are avoiding.
formulas.purpose: A memorable handle people can repeat to someone else.
formulas.ruins: A rule that is really three rules.

formulas.name: The Forecast
formulas.template: By {year}, {prediction}. Here is what to do now.
formulas.example: By 2028 most entry-level security work will look different. Here is what to do now.
formulas.purpose: Future stakes plus a present action.
formulas.ruins: A prediction with no action attached.

formulas.name: Someone Else's Result
formulas.template: My {student, client, friend} {result} using {method}.
formulas.example: My cousin cracked a scholarship interview using one practice rule.
formulas.purpose: Social proof without bragging. Easier to believe than your own win.
formulas.ruins: Results you cannot name, even anonymously.

formulas.name: The Superlative
formulas.template: The {best or worst} {thing} I have ever {verb}.
formulas.example: The worst advice I have ever followed about college applications.
formulas.purpose: Extreme claims get attention. The story under it earns the retention.
formulas.ruins: A superlative the story does not support.

formulas.name: The Quiet Part
formulas.template: Nobody says this out loud, but {truth}.
formulas.example: Nobody says this out loud, but most scholarship essays are won in the first two lines.
formulas.purpose: Permission to hear something uncomfortable.
formulas.ruins: A truth that is not uncomfortable.

dealbreakers.message: Greeting. Nobody opened the feed to be greeted.
Asking for attention proves you have not earned it. Say the thing instead.

dealbreakers.rx: \b(in this video|in today'?s video|today i('?m| am| want| wanted)|today we('?re| are| will)|i wanted to (talk|share|show)|let me (tell|show) you about|before we (start|begin|get started)|welcome back)\b
dealbreakers.message: Preamble. Announcing the video is not the video.
A subscribe plea in the hook. Earn it at the end.

warnings.message: Hype word. Replace with the specific thing that is crazy.

warnings.rx: \b(kind of|sort of|maybe|i think|i guess|a little bit)\b
warnings.message: Hedging in the hook. State it like you mean it or cut it.
